description: pyCSEP is a Python toolkit for testing earthquake forecasts against observed earthquake catalogues. Its own README describes forecast formats, evaluation routines and benchmark models used by CSEP testing centres. The JOSS paper names the toolkit as the software resource, although its JATS summary endpoint returned 404 during this review. Spatial coverage is the forecast region and temporal coverage is the forecast and test period selected by a user. The public repository reports BSD-3-Clause. It can help compare seismic-hazard forecasts before they feed asset-exposure or resilience simulations. A caveat is that statistical forecast skill is not a direct estimate of earthquake damage at a building or network. Catalogue completeness and forecast windows affect tests. No matching catalogue or first-review resource was found. The JOSS landing page and own repository were checked without obtaining an earthquake catalogue or running an experiment.
name: pyCSEP earthquake forecast evaluation
notes: G5 G5-0774. Software checked through metadata and documentation, without installation or execution. Geographic scope follows the documented application or software portability; it does not imply validation throughout that area.
